jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

CAPCOA seeks a collaborative and politically experienced and astute Executive Director to lead the organization’s next chapter and ensure that California’s local air districts continue to have an effective, credible, and coordinated statewide voice.

The Executive Director serves as CAPCOA’s chief executive and is responsible for strategic leadership, Board and member engagement, policy development and advocacy, government relations, financial and grant oversight, organizational administration, and staff leadership. The position requires an executive who can operate independently while remaining closely accountable to the Board and responsive to the membership.

This is both a strategic and hands\-on role. The successful candidate will be able to advise senior public officials on complex air quality issues, facilitate agreement among diverse member agencies, effectively represent CAPCOA in high\-level policy settings, and ensure that the daily work of a small association—including budgets, grants, contracts, meetings, communications, and personnel—is managed with discipline and care.

**Position and Reporting Relationship**

The Executive Director reports to a 14\-member Board of Directors composed of air pollution control officers from throughout California and works closely with the Board President and Executive Committee. The Executive Director exercises substantial independence within Board\-approved policies, organizational bylaws, adopted policy positions, and the annual work plan.

The Executive Director supervises CAPCOA staff, provides direction to consultants and contractors, coordinates with CAPCOA’s Chief Financial Officer and accounting providers, and supports committees and workgroups composed largely of personnel from member air districts.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Initial Leadership Priorities***

· Maintain organizational continuity and member confidence during the leadership transition.

· Strengthen engagement and trust across large, medium, small, urban, and rural air districts.

· Ensure disciplined oversight of CAPCOA’s finances, grants, contracts, audits, and pass\-through funding.

· Improve CAPCOA’s ability to anticipate, prioritize, and respond to legislative, regulatory, funding, and program developments.

· Evaluate staffing, administrative systems, communications, member services, and consultant support to ensure they align with the organization’s priorities.

· Work with the Board and membership to define CAPCOA’s strategic direction and annual work plan for the next phase of statewide leadership.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Strategic Leadership and Policy***

· Advise the Board and membership on emerging federal, state, and local air quality issues, including their practical, legal, financial, and operational implications for local air districts.

· Lead development and implementation of CAPCOA’s strategic priorities, annual work plan, and Board\-directed initiatives.

· Coordinate development of timely, technically credible policy positions that accurately reflect Board and membership direction.

· Recommend the appropriate CAPCOA committee, workgroup, member representative, consultant, or staff resource to evaluate and respond to priority issues.

· Identify organizational risks, emerging opportunities, and issues requiring coordinated statewide action.

***Board and Member Leadership***

· Build trusted relationships with air pollution control officers and staff from all 35 member agencies.

· Support effective Board and Executive Committee decision\-making through clear analysis, practical recommendations, accurate records, and reliable follow\-through.

· Facilitate consensus when member agencies have differing priorities, circumstances, or policy perspectives while preserving the value of local flexibility.

· Plan and support Board meetings, membership meetings, retreats, conferences, committees, workgroups, and other Board\-directed activities.

· Respond to member inquiries and connect districts with relevant information, expertise, resources, and peer support.

· Ensure that CAPCOA remains responsive to districts of varying size, geography, staffing, and technical capacity.

***Government, Legislative, and External Affairs***

· Serve as CAPCOA’s principal liaison with CARB, CalEPA, the U.S. EPA, the Legislature, and other governmental partners.

· Direct and implement legislative and regulatory advocacy consistent with positions approved by the Board and membership.

· Represent CAPCOA and elevate its policy positions in public meetings, hearings, conferences, stakeholder processes, and high\-level policy forums.

· Prepare or oversee clear, timely written comments, policy statements, testimony, correspondence, presentations, newsletters, and other communications.

· Develop constructive relationships with industry, environmental, community, tribal, public\-interest, academic, and professional organizations as appropriate to CAPCOA’s mission.

· Communicate complex technical and policy matters in a manner that is accurate, accessible, and responsive to the intended audience.

***Financial, Grant, and Contract Stewardship***

· Oversee preparation and implementation of CAPCOA’s annual budget and long\-term financial planning.

· Ensure accurate and timely financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable and receivable, audits, tax filings, and compliance with applicable requirements.

· Coordinate closely with CAPCOA’s Chief Financial Officer, accounting providers, auditors, legal counsel, and other professional advisors.

· Secure, administer, track, and report on grants received by CAPCOA, including funds passed through to member districts or other recipients.

· Ensure compliance with grant conditions, federal and state requirements, contracts, procurement expectations, and restrictions on public funds.

Identify, cultivate, and recognize leadership from farmworkers and low\-income families to expand opportunities in their lives.

**OUR VISION**

CCA envisions farmworkers, low\-income families, and youth leading neighborhood\-based committees (comités) that successfully advocate for improved housing, health, and economic conditions and opportunities for our community. CCA envisions a strengthened social fabric of our community through alliances and the development of community leaders.

**CORE VALUES**

**Inclusiveness:** CCA is dedicated to promoting an environment in which communities provide resources that foster leadership development among farmworkers such that they serve as leaders and participate in community building and decision making.

**Company Description** **Deputy Director,** **Multifamily Housing and Homeownership Programs**  



**Classification: 0904 Mayoral Staff XVI**  

**Department: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)**  

**Reports To: Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development Director**


Reporting directly to the MOHCD Director, the **Deputy Director, Multifamily Housing and Homeownership Programs** provides executive leadership for the City’s affordable multifamily housing production, preservation, housing finance, construction oversight, and homeownership programs. In coordination with the Director, the Deputy Director establishes the strategic direction for these program areas, oversees policy development and implementation, and advances innovative financing and programmatic initiatives that expand affordable housing opportunities and sustainable homeownership throughout San Francisco.


The Deputy Director provides executive oversight of the Homeownership and Multifamily Rental Housing Division that includes 38 staff members.


Additionally, the Deputy Director provides direct supervision to 5 Director\-level leadership staff responsible for these major program areas:

* New Construction
* Acquisition and Preservation
* Housing Finance
* Homeownership Programs
* Construction Representation

**New Construction**


MOHCD’s New Construction Program is led by a Director who manages a team of project managers and loan administrators responsible for developing 100 percent affordable housing throughout San Francisco. Responsibilities include underwriting projects for approval by the Citywide Loan Committee and Board of Supervisors; overseeing affordable housing development partners during programming, predevelopment, construction, marketing, and lease\-up; administering the City’s Land Dedication Program; and closing construction and permanent financing.

**Acquisition and Preservation**


The Acquisition and Preservation Program is led by a Director responsible for financing the acquisition, rehabilitation, and long\-term preservation of affordable multifamily housing. The program oversees refinancing and restructuring of existing affordable housing developments, administers the Small Sites Program, coordinates acquisition financing strategies, and partners with nonprofit developers, lenders, and public agencies to preserve affordable housing throughout the City.

**Housing Finance**


The Housing Finance Director is responsible for coordinating MOHCD’s multifamily financing and underwriting activities, including affordable housing revenue bonds, loan structuring, lending policies, capital financing strategies, and funding procurements. The Director evaluates federal, state, and local financing opportunities to maximize affordable housing resources and develops policies that strengthen the City’s affordable housing investment strategies.

**Homeownership Programs**


MOHCD’s Homeownership Programs are led by a Director responsible for the City’s affordable homeownership initiatives, including Inclusionary ownership programs within market rate housing and the sale and re\-sale of Below Market Rate (BMR) units, first\-time homeowner assistance programs, and related affordable homeownership opportunities. The Director oversees the secondary lending activities and administration of all homebuyer and homeowner loan programs including loan servicing of approximately 850 market rate property loans. Creating an average of 200 new first\-time homeowners each year, the Director oversees the implementation of all homeownership programs generated by the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) and other affordable homeownership initiatives designed to expand equitable access to homeownership. The Director works closely with the Homeownership Compliance Manager to ensure households purchasing market rate housing with City assistance remain program eligible throughout their ownership. The Director develops and implements policies, oversees program operations, and collaborates with lenders, nonprofit organizations, developers, community\-based organizations, and public agencies to advance the City’s affordable homeownership goals.

**Construction Representation**


A Senior Construction Representative manages a team of construction professionals responsible for evaluating MOHCD\-funded projects throughout all phases of development to ensure cost efficiency, constructability, and compliance with program and design standards. The team monitors projects during construction through project closeout and works collaboratively with project sponsors and regulatory agencies to resolve development issues.

**About the Ventura County Community Foundation**

The Ventura County Community Foundation stewards more than $285 million in charitable assets on behalf of individuals, families, and organizations who love this community. We describe ourselves as keepers of the dream. Donors trust us with their charitable dreams, and we keep those dreams alive with care, discipline, and integrity across generations. Our work is connecting people, resources, and solutions to build lasting impact in our shared world.

We are a small team carrying a large mandate. That combination makes this a role of unusual reach. The person in this seat sits at the center of a foundation working on early childhood education, local journalism, guaranteed income, disaster resilience, and the long\-term financial security of the nonprofits that hold this county together.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Assistant works in a close one\-on\-one partnership with the President \& CEO and serves as the primary point of contact for internal and external constituencies on all matters pertaining to the Office of the President. The role protects the CEO’s time, anticipates what is coming, and makes sure nothing of consequence falls through.

This is not a task\-taking position. The Executive Assistant exercises independent judgment daily, holds confidential information belonging to donors, board members, and team members, and represents the Foundation to some of the most significant philanthropic and civic leaders in the region. The right person is unusually organized, calm under pressure, quick to learn, and genuinely interested in the mission.

The Executive Assistant is also the steward of “Home Plate”, the daily operating system that keeps the CEO’s office and the leadership team aligned. Maintaining that rhythm is a core function of the role, not an add\-on.

**What Success Looks Like**

By the end of the first year, the Executive Assistant will have:

* Earned the full trust of the President \& CEO, the Board Chair, and the leadership team, and become the person everyone calls first.
* Taken ownership of Home Plate so that daily priorities, follow\-ups, and commitments move without prompting.
* Built a calendar and travel practice that reflects real strategic priorities rather than the order in which requests arrive.

* Communicates directly, and on behalf of the President \& CEO, with board members, donors, professional advisors, nonprofit partners, elected officials, and team members.
* Researches, prioritizes, and follows up on incoming issues addressed to the President, including those of a sensitive or confidential nature, and determines the appropriate course of action, referral, or response.
* Keeps the President \& CEO well informed of upcoming commitments and responsibilities. Acts as a barometer for the issues moving through the organization and the community, and surfaces them early.
* Drafts acknowledgement letters, personal correspondence, briefing notes, and meeting recaps that are ready to send with minimal editing.
* Prioritizes competing needs, handles matters expeditiously and proactively, and follows through to completion under real deadline pressure.

**Board and Governance Support**

* Supports board members with travel, lodging, and meeting arrangements as needed.

**About NYC Kids RISE**


Over the last decade, NYC Kids RISE has been working alongside partners in government, philanthropy, business and communities to build a first\-of\-its\-kind universal community wealth building platform for New York City neighborhoods.


Through the Program, nearly every public school student in New York City has an NYC Scholarship Account, starting in kindergarten, with money already invested in a 529 college savings plan, and opportunities to earn more money through rewards and Community Scholarships. Today, more than 380,000 students have NYC Scholarship Accounts with more than \~$85 million designated for their educational futures. The Program is on pace to reach nearly all \~1 million NYC public school students by 2034\.


The Program expands access to mainstream financial products; builds individual, family, and collective financial assets; provides financial education for families and students; and brings schools and communities together to support all their children’s futures. As a unique vehicle for building both financial and social capital, the platform serves as a model for generational wealth building and fostering neighborhoods of economic opportunity — locally and nationally — especially for families who have historically faced barriers to wealth building.


In June, the City announced an historic investment, increasing the initial seed scholarship for kindergartners from $100 to $1,000\. With growing national, state, and local bipartisan recognition of the power of early wealth building and our infrastructure in place, there is a window of tremendous opportunity to realize a bold vision for New York City kids.


Learn more about NYC Kids RISE at nyckidsrise.org.

About the Agency:  

  

  

  

  

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3\.7 million homes in New York City.  

  

  

  

  

As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.
  

  

Your Team:  

  

  

  

The Office of Development (OOD) leads the agency’s effort to create and preserve affordable housing in collaboration with other HPD offices as well as other city, state and federal agencies. The OOD is comprised of eight divisions that administer a range of programs. These divisions include Portfolio Management \& Conversions, New Construction Finance, Special Needs Housing, Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), Homeownership Opportunities and Preservation, Preservation Finance, Compliance and Enforcement, and Housing Incentives.
  

  

The Division of Portfolio Management \& Conversions (PMC) manages development projects after closing with an initial loan to manage rent restructuring and conversion to permanent financing, to deploy rental assistance to tenants prior to project stabilization, to ensure projects’ adherence to program and accounting requirements, and to facilitate timely completion. As a relatively new division in the OOD, PMC administers multiple programs areas including Conversions \& Rental Assistance, Requisitions, and Construction Monitoring \& Completions.
  

Within OOD, PMC collaborates especially closely with the Division of Preservation Finance (PF) on a substantial shared portfolio of projects. As a result, PMC and PF share additional executive and operational support, including an Associate Commissioner and an Executive Director of Policy and Operations, that support both divisions.
  

Program Areas within the Division:
  

The Conversions team oversees the conversion of construction loans to permanent financing, a critical checkpoint for HPD to ensure that development teams have adhered to program requirements, and to set up these projects for long\-term success for decades to come. The unit also oversees rent restructuring, a process through which HPD resets rents in a project in accordance with various laws, regulations, and program policies, and which is a critical tool to ensure housing affordability and long\-term project stability. All of this involves managing due diligence requirements, managing multiple external stakeholders to overcome barriers to achieving these milestones, establishing new rent\-stabilized rents, and close coordination with a broad array of HPD staff.
  

  

The Rental Assistance team plays a key role in ensuring tenants in HPD\-financed affordable housing are able to access rental assistance, and that projects reach rental achievement targets in a timely manner in order to convert to permanent financing. This work includes direct outreach and assistance to tenants, reviewing tenant income certifications for projects that provide preferential rent offers, and close coordination with the Division of Tenant and Owner Resources around the provision of rental assistance to eligible households.

jobs.description:
The **Executive Director for Corporate Sponsorship and Engagement** serves as the university's senior leader responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing a coordinated institutional strategy for corporate engagement, sponsorship, and revenue\-generating partnerships.


Reporting to the Vice President for External Relations, the Executive Director will establish and lead the Office of Corporate Sponsorship and Engagement and serve as the university's central point of coordination for corporate partnerships. The position will work collaboratively across academic, healthcare, student life, research, advancement, athletics, and administrative units to create a comprehensive framework that protects institutional interests while generating new revenue opportunities and enhancing the student experience. Athletics and the University of Iowa Center for Advancement will be key partners but will retain responsibility for athletics sponsorships and corporate philanthropic engagement, respectively.


The Executive Director will build the infrastructure, governance, policies, valuation methodologies, and partner development strategies necessary to support long\-term growth in corporate sponsorship revenue while maintaining alignment with the university's mission and values.


This position is a 3\-year term appointment, subject to reappointment pending resources generated from new sponsorship activities.


There is an expectation that the person in this position will maintain effective, civil, and respectful working relationships with the University of Iowa campus community and uphold the University’s commitment to creating welcoming and respectful environments for all.


The position is primarily on\-site could have the possiblity of hybrid in the future.


This position is eligible for hybrid work within Iowa and will require a work arrangement form to be completed upon the start of your employment. * Develop and manage relationships with regional, national, and global corporate partners.
* Create sponsorship packages and partnership opportunities that leverage institutional assets.

**Governance and Risk Management**

* Establish, chair and coordinate a Sponsorship Review Committee.
* Ensure appropriate review and approval of sponsorship agreements.

* Lead development of institutional asset inventories and valuation methodologies.

* Serve as the university's primary coordinator for corporate engagement activities.
* Build collaborative relationships across advancement, colleges, divisions, centers, healthcare, and administrative units.

**Financial and Operational Oversight**

* Develop and manage the Office of Corporate Sponsorship and Engagement budget.
* Establish performance metrics and reporting systems.

* **Experience within higher education, healthcare, athletics, or nonprofit organizations.**
* **Experience establishing new organizational functions or revenue\-generating initiatives.**

Position Type: Part\-Time contract (22\-25 hours/week), with potential to transition to Full\-Time

engagement with our tribal nations. This role is ideal for a professional dedicated to empowering Tribal  

tourism entrepreneurs, preserving cultural heritage, and unifying tourism initiatives across the nine  

federally recognized Tribal Nations in South Dakota. The Director works directly with the Administrative  

Specialist and reports to the Board of Directors.  

  

Core Priorities \& Responsibilities
  

1\. Strategic Project Management \& Tourism Development (50%)  

* Event Production: Manage planning, logistics, scheduling, and implementation of community training, and all programs and events. Assist Consultant Specialist with SDNTA board meetings. Develop community\-based outreach and education initiatives.
* Community Collaboration: Build our partnerships with Tribal communities, Economic Development Committees, South Dakota Tourism Department and Native\-owned businesses to identify, plan, and implement culturally sensitive, sustainable tourism offerings. Will be the boots\-on\-the\-ground for all events and programs. Build out a volunteer engagement and inclusion program that involves Youth Leaders.
* Grant Execution: Assist in delivering priority projects identified by SDNTA’s Programs \& Advocacy Team in strict alignment with grant goals and deliverables. Assist in managing the project budgets and reporting when needed.
* Tour Operations: Pilot existing tour experiences and contribute to designing an SDNTA\-managed tour operation model to coordinate and promote Native\-led itineraries and communities. Work directly with Tribal nations for input and communication for project direction and priorities.

2\. Operations, Logistics \& Grant Compliance (20%)  

  

* Daily Administration: Will be responsible for answering organizational inquiries from the website while working with the Board of Directors to assist in answering these inquiries in a timely manner. Will help maintain official files, records, and digital assets. Assist with administrative tasks when needed.
* Data Tracking: Gather project and program metrics, track participant attendance, and compile impact data to assist with grant compliance and reporting as well as to help with future technical info required for success. Create a shared database, updated group text and updated group email chains for the Board of Directors.
* Budget Support: Assist leadership and consultant in monitoring project budgets and preparing documentation for upcoming grant proposals and monthly reviews.

3\. Partnership Development \& Communication (30%)  

  

* Tribal Engagement: Build and maintain trusted relationships with Tribal leaders, government agencies, and grassroots partners across South Dakota's Tribal Nations. Task is to reconnect in a partnership with each of the nine Tribal councils and individual organizations by engaging in\-person visits. Set up quarterly meetings and provide quarterly reports to the tribes.
* Network Outreach: Assist in conducting community outreach to expand SDNTA’s network, ensuring equitable representation and identifying local points of contact in each Tribal Nation. Work directly with SD Tourism and Tribal Relations and Economic Development to help define partnership and continue to build progress.
* Public Relations: Support marketing and storytelling efforts by drafting community newsletters, social media content, and press releases. Work with Administrative Specialist to update SDNTA website to include accomplishments, press coverage and news coverage and assist in marketing strategies for entrepreneurs. Will help create and launch a Marketing \& Media Committee to help SDNTA to present promotional materials to support our tribal nations and the people.
* Representation: Will represent SDNTA at conferences, events and meetings to advance awareness of the organization’s mission.

Full\-time \| Exempt \| Reports to the ownership \| Target start: October/November 2026

**About CIS**

Community Integrated Services (CIS) is a New Hampshire provider of residential, day, case management, and specialty services for adults with developmental disabilities and acquired brain disorders. We are funded through the NH Bureau of Developmental Services (BDS) waiver system and work in partnership with the state's Area Agencies. CIS is part of a family of agencies serving northern New England for nearly three decades, with roots in New Hampshire going back to 1997\. CIS has a larger sister agency that operates in Maine, both of which receive administrative oversight from a centralized office located in Concord NH.

**The Opportunity**

CIS is hiring an Executive Director to manage all operations in New Hampshire. The Executive Director sets the strategic direction for CIS, executes it through a leadership team of Area Directors and department heads, builds relationships with NH DHHS, BDS, BEAS, the Area Agencies, families, guardians, and community partners, and is accountable for the agency’s quality, compliance, and financial results.

You will step into a stable, well\-supported agency with strong systems and an engaged leadership team, backed by the shared resources of our parent organization. The Executive Director will build on that foundation and focus on what comes next: growing the agency, developing new revenue streams, deepening our partnerships across New Hampshire, and leading a team that delivers quality services every day.

**What You Will Do**

Set direction and lead

* Develop the strategic plan for CIS with input from ownership, the leadership team, and the people we support; translate it into annual goals and execute it through your team.

* Supervise the team responsible for service authorizations, utilization, and billing, and act on the trends they report.
* Identify and pursue new revenue streams and service lines that fit the agency’s mission and capacity.

* Lead the agency’s responses to referrals and RFPs; open new programs and close under\-performing ones responsibly.

* Ensure clinical, nursing, and behavioral\-support departments are led by qualified, properly credentialed staff and meet agency standards for timeliness and quality.
* Oversee the after\-hours on\-call system and provide crisis coordination when needed.
